title: Pulsar game manifest (schema version 1)
description: Describes how Pulsar installs, starts, watches and stops a game server. Declarative and closed: there is no shell, script or expression anywhere. Pulsar validates more than this schema can express (placeholders, regular expressions, paths); see docs/architecture/04-game-manifests.md.

key.description: Identifies the game; with the version, a template that never changes.

version.description: Semantic version of this manifest's content.

install.description: Steps run when the server is installed or reinstalled.

update.description: Steps run when the game is updated. Without them, updates are not offered.

addons.description: Mods the game supports, installed on request.

mods.description: Catalogs of mods the panel installs files from (Pulsar 1.0.9).

license.description: As the addon's authors state it; shown before installing.

target.description: Folder of the server the archive is unpacked into (a relative path, with its rules); empty for the server's folder.

reinstallAfterUpdate.description: The game's updates overwrite it: its latest release is installed again after each update.

GitHubReleaseSource.description: A zip asset of a GitHub release, checked against the SHA-256 GitHub publishes for it. A fixed 'tag' cannot go with 'prerelease': true (that only picks the newest release).

asset.description: Regular expression for the asset's file name.

tag.description: A fixed release; the latest one without it.

prerelease.description: Take the newest release even when it is marked as a pre-release.

LineEdit.description: Keeps 'line' right after the first line of 'path' that reads 'after' (spaces aside), before every start.

RequirementsDefinition.description: Shown when a server is created; not enforced.

type.description: number: a decimal ("1.5"), up to 6 decimals.

default.description: A scalar; its text is checked like a value users enter.

secret.description: Encrypted at rest, write-only in the API, masked in the UI and logs. String variables only, without a default.

pattern.description: Non-backtracking regular expression; required for strings used in arguments or configuration files.

min.description: Integer and number variables; whole for integers.

max.description: Integer and number variables; whole for integers.

WorkshopList.description: The variable lists Steam Workshop item ids; the panel offers an editor that looks them up on Steam.

appId.description: The game's Steam app id (whose Workshop the items are in).

required.description: Optional ports can only be used inside { "if": "port.<name>" } arguments.

internal.description: Only the agent uses it, on this machine (a game's telnet console): never opened in the firewall.

PortFollow.description: The game opens this port at a fixed distance from another (Valheim: the game port + 1): it gets the allocation of the same address at that port.

SteamCmdStep.description: Installs or updates a Steam app with SteamCMD, as the server's own account.

login.description: 'account': only a Steam account that owns the dedicated server may download it; the server needs one set in the panel.

betaPasswordVar.description: A secret variable holding the beta branch password. The agent fails the install (steamcmd.beta_password_invalid) when its value is one SteamCMD would not receive whole: more than 64 characters, spaces, double quotes or control characters, or a leading + or -.

TestGameServerStep.description: Pulsar's own test game server; only for the pulsar-test manifest.

MinecraftServerStep.description: Minecraft: Java Edition's server.jar from Mojang and the Java runtime its version needs in java/ (Eclipse Temurin), both checked against their publishers' checksums; or (Pulsar 1.0.9) Paper, Purpur, Fabric, Forge or NeoForge.

versionVar.description: A variable holding the version ('1.21.4', or 'latest' for the latest release).

typeVar.description: An enum variable choosing the server type (Pulsar 1.0.9): vanilla, paper, purpur, fabric, forge or neoforge.

loaderVar.description: A variable holding the version of Fabric's loader, Forge or NeoForge; empty for the recommended one (Pulsar 1.0.9).

MinecraftBedrockStep.description: Minecraft: Bedrock Edition's dedicated server for Windows from Mojang (Pulsar 1.0.8), its bedrock_server.exe accepted only signed by Microsoft; an update keeps server.properties, allowlist.json, permissions.json and packetlimitconfig.json.

versionVar.description: A variable holding the version ('1.21.50.07', or 'latest' for the latest release).

CopyFileIfMissingStep.description: Copies a file of the server directory to 'to' when that does not exist yet (a game's shipped settings as the server's own).

ArgumentTemplate.description: One argv element, with {{var.<key>}}, {{var.<key>.<sub>}}, {{port.<name>}}, {{port.<name>.ip}}, {{rcon.password}}, {{server.shortId}} or {{server.dir}} placeholders, or a conditional group.

if.description: A variable (a boolean when true, any other when it has a value), what an enum's chosen option maps when it is not empty (Pulsar 1.0.9), or an optional port (assigned).

else.description: What goes instead when the condition does not hold.

mode.description: pty: pseudo console; pipes: redirected stdio; logfile+rcon: output from a log file, commands through RCON (Source engine on Windows).

port.description: Name of a required port; RCON listens on its TCP side, which only needs to be reachable from the node.

logsCommands.description: The game writes commands received over RCON to its log file, so the console does not add them again; an answer is added only when the log does not show it.

protocol.description: a2s: Valve's server queries over UDP (Source and most Steam games); minecraft: the Server List Ping over TCP.

port.description: Name of a required port with the protocol's transport (UDP for a2s, TCP for minecraft).

CommandsDefinition.description: Console commands the panel sends for the game's players (Pulsar 1.0.9; players 1.0.11), through the server's console or RCON.

broadcast.description: Tells everyone playing a message: {{message}} stands for it (say {{message}}). The panel keeps only letters, digits, spaces and . , ! ? : ' ( ) - of a message.

messageSpaces.description: What stands for a space in the message, for a game whose command takes one word.

PlayerCommandsDefinition.description: What the panel does to one player (Pulsar 1.0.11): each command has {{player}} once where the player goes. The panel refuses a player that is not 1 to 64 letters, digits and _ - . (and single spaces, with 'spaces'); it never cleans one.

kick.description: Puts the player out of the game (kick {{player}}).

ban.description: Keeps the player out for good.

unban.description: Lets a banned player in again.

whitelistAdd.description: Adds the player to the list of who may join.

whitelistRemove.description: Takes the player off that list.

adminAdd.description: Makes the player the game's operator or admin (the panel asks for the right to send console commands too).

byId.description: The commands take an id (a Steam ID), not the name the game's query lists.

spaces.description: A name may have spaces: the commands' arguments do not end at one (quoted, or ended by another character).

PlayerListsDefinition.description: The game's files listing who is banned, on its whitelist, or its admins, for the panel to show.

PlayerListFile.description: A JSON file holding an array of objects, each naming a player in 'field' (Minecraft's ops.json).

ModSourceDefinition.description: A catalog of mods (Pulsar 1.0.9): what a server of each type takes from it, and where.

versionVar.description: The variable holding the game's version, when the install does not report it.

typeVar.description: The enum variable holding the server's type; each type the catalog serves is a key of 'types'.

ModpacksDefinition.description: The catalog's modpacks install on the game: a pack runs on the type whose mods it is made of, at the game version it names.

loaderVar.description: The string variable holding the loader's version, which the pack's index names.

loaders.description: The catalog's loaders a file must be for, any of them.

folder.description: The server's folder the files go into.

format.description: colon: key: value per line, # comments (SCP: Secret Laboratory). space: Key value per line, // comments (Unturned). json: members of a JSON object, each key a JSON Pointer (/gameSettings/enemyDamageFactor); patch mode only.

mode.description: patch: only the declared keys change; managed: the whole file is written by Pulsar.

section.description: unreal-ini: the [section] the keys go into, without its brackets. xml-properties: the root element.

struct.description: unreal-ini: the keys are members of this Struct=(Key=Value,...) line instead of plain lines.

keepIfEmpty.description: Keys of set whose line stays as the file has it when their value is empty (an option left unset); an empty value of another key removes its line.

writeIfEmpty.description: json only: keys of set whose empty value is written as an empty string instead of removing the member.

timeoutSeconds.description: After it, the agent kills the whole process tree.

include.description: Globs relative to the server directory. Without them, everything is included.

GameSaveDefinition.description: Console commands that make a running game save before a backup captures its files.

commands.description: Sent in order through the server's console (RCON when the console uses it).

confirmation.description: Non-backtracking regular expression: the console line that says the save ended.

waitSeconds.description: How long to wait after the commands when there is no confirmation.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait for the confirmation (default 60).

resume.description: Sent once the files are captured, to undo what the commands paused.

RelativePath.description: Relative to the server directory, with forward slashes; no empty, '.' or '..' segments, root, drive or stream, no Windows device names (CON, NUL, COM1…), no name that starts with a space or ends with a dot or a space, no control characters, nothing in Pulsar's own .pulsar folder, names of up to 255 characters.
